## Simple explanation

Similarity search finds items that resemble a query. An image or text can
be represented as a vector, and a search system returns items with nearby
or similarly oriented vectors.

## Technical explanation

Given a query vector and an indexed collection, similarity search ranks
candidates using a metric such as cosine similarity, dot product, or
Euclidean distance. Exact search compares against all vectors; approximate
nearest-neighbor indexes trade exactness for speed and memory.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Vector similarity search is used in semantic retrieval, recommendations,
duplicate detection, and RAG. The embedding model, normalization, metric,
index parameters, and data distribution jointly affect relevance and
performance.

## How it works

An encoder maps items and queries to vectors. The index searches for
nearest neighbors under the configured metric and returns ranked candidates.
Systems often apply metadata filters or rerank the candidates using
additional signals.

## Practical example

A product catalog can encode descriptions and retrieve products near a
customer's text query. Evaluate results with human relevance judgments and
measure index recall and latency at realistic catalog sizes.

## Common misconceptions

- Geometrically close vectors are not guaranteed to be semantically
  relevant for every use case.
- Approximate nearest-neighbor search may miss true nearest neighbors; its
  recall-performance trade-off should be measured.
